# susfs4ksu-lkm-x64

x86_64 port of [inforcqb/susfs4ksu-lkm](https://github.com/inforcqb/susfs4ksu-lkm): susfs as a loadable kernel module for the Android 16 x86_64 emulator image, whose kernel comes from the android15-6.6 branch (6.6.66-android15-8), running beside KernelSU-Next LKM. No custom kernel, nothing replaces the ramdisk. Please use [KernelSU-Next-AVD](https://github.com/ymuuuu/KernelSU-Next-AVD) to root your AVD. Releases and updates are announced on Telegram: [t.me/ymuulabs](https://t.me/ymuulabs). ## Added in this fork Features this fork has on top of upstream, beyond the x86_64 port itself. Details: [PROC_INTERFACES.en.md](PROC_INTERFACES.en.md). | Feature | What it does | How to use | Since | |---|---|---|---| | `no_reverse` | The open is still redirected, but the redirected-to file's name is not swapped back to the original in `maps`, fd links, fdinfo and `statfs()`. | Rule word on `add_open_redirect` | v0.0.7 | | `app_only` | The redirect applies only to app processes (executable `/system/bin/app_process64` or `app_process32`). Root, shell and other processes open the real file. | Rule word on `add_open_redirect` | v0.0.8 | | `keep_ident` | A file the rule opened reports the original's `st_dev` and `st_ino`, so `fstat()` on the fd matches `stat()` on the path. `readlink` of the own `/proc/self/fd/N` returns the original path. | Rule word on `add_open_redirect` | v0.0.8 | | Redirect target exempt from sus_path | A redirect's own open of its target is not blocked when the target is also a sus_path. | Automatic | v0.0.8 | | `/proc/susfs_uname_machine` | `uname()` reports the given `machine` only to processes that map the marker file (translated arm64 apps). | `set ` / `clear` | v0.0.8 | | `/proc/susfs_prop_view` | When a process becomes an app (at `setresuid`), its mapping of a property area file is replaced with a copy at the same address. Root, shell and non-app processes keep the real area. | `add ` / `clear` | v0.0.8 | ## Build Pushes to main run four jobs: `arm64-control` (upstream module, unchanged, catches regressions), `x86_64-port` (this port, android15-6.6), `x86_64-matrix` (the other KMIs the KernelSU-Next CI covers, android12-5.10 up to android17-6.18) and `x86_64-package`. All must be green. Artifacts per run: `x86_64-android15-6.6-susfs_guard_lkm.ko`, the per-KMI `x86_64--susfs_guard_lkm.ko` set, `x86_64-susfs_sc` (bare supercall test client) and `x86_64-susfs-lkm-module` (the flashable loader module zip, one .ko per KMI, the boot script picks by kernel release). Prebuilt binaries: the [releases](https://github.com/ymuuuu/susfs4ksu-lkm-x64/releases) page. ## Install The module zip is the intended path: KernelSU-Next manager, module section, install from storage, reboot (or `ksud module install susfs_lkm_x64.zip`). After reboot the module loads itself at boot and installs the x86_64 `susfs` CLI at `/data/adb/ksu/bin/susfs` (with `sus` and `ksu_susfs` symlinks) for manager modules that call the classic command line. Check with `ksud susfs version`, expect v2.3.0. For a manual one-shot load instead: plain `insmod` cannot work, five imports are unexported to modules on every GKI variant, arm64 included, same as upstream. Use `ksud insmod `. The module hides itself from lsmod on purpose; check `/sys/module/susfs_guard_lkm` instead. ## State Live-tested on the emulator: autoload after reboot, `ksud susfs version` answers v2.3.0 and `ksud susfs support` answers Supported, sus_path hides paths from app uids while root and shell still see them, uname spoof, kstat/opath/open_redirect tables, no-opt probes holding. v1 scope: the AArch32 compat layer stays arm64-only. ![image.png](image.png) Userspace talks through the reboot-ABI supercall and the `/proc/susfs_*` nodes (interface reference: upstream [PROC_INTERFACES.md](https://github.com/inforcqb/susfs4ksu-lkm/blob/main/PROC_INTERFACES.md)). > IMPORTANT: Manager modules that ship their own arm64 `susfs`/`ksu_susfs` binaries (BRENE, sidex15) still carry a dead arm64 binary inside; the installed CLI here answers the same command surface, but those modules' installers may need their arch gate bypassed. Short Answer: susfs4ksu-module and all its forks still needs to be ported to x86_64 ## Origin and license Port of inforcqb/susfs4ksu-lkm, which ports simonpunk/susfs4ksu (logic and hook points), with patch_memory/lsm_hook/symbol_resolver from SukiSU-Ultra. GPL-2.0-only, see LICENSE. Research and learning only, use at your own risk. ## Disclaimer I am no developer or a low level programmer, I am a guy who loves breaking, testing, building security releated tools that helps with my workflow, excpect bugs and errors, thank you.
readmeHTML:
susfs4ksu-lkm-x64

x86_64 port of inforcqb/susfs4ksu-lkm: susfs as a loadable kernel module for the Android 16 x86_64 emulator image, whose kernel comes from the android15-6.6 branch (6.6.66-android15-8), running beside KernelSU-Next LKM. No custom kernel, nothing replaces the ramdisk.

Please use KernelSU-Next-AVD to root your AVD.

Releases and updates are announced on Telegram: t.me/ymuulabs.

Added in this fork

Features this fork has on top of upstream, beyond the x86_64 port itself. Details: PROC_INTERFACES.en.md.

| Feature | What it does | How to use | Since |

|---|---|---|---|

| no_reverse | The open is still redirected, but the redirected-to file's name is not swapped back to the original in maps, fd links, fdinfo and statfs(). | Rule word on add_open_redirect | v0.0.7 |

| app_only | The redirect applies only to app processes (executable /system/bin/app_process64 or app_process32). Root, shell and other processes open the real file. | Rule word on add_open_redirect | v0.0.8 |

| keep_ident | A file the rule opened reports the original's st_dev and st_ino, so fstat() on the fd matches stat() on the path. readlink of the own /proc/self/fd/N returns the original path. | Rule word on add_open_redirect | v0.0.8 |

| Redirect target exempt from sus_path | A redirect's own open of its target is not blocked when the target is also a sus_path. | Automatic | v0.0.8 |

| /proc/susfs_uname_machine | uname() reports the given machine only to processes that map the marker file (translated arm64 apps). | set / clear | v0.0.8 |

| /proc/susfs_prop_view | When a process becomes an app (at setresuid), its mapping of a property area file is replaced with a copy at the same address. Root, shell and non-app processes keep the real area. | add / clear | v0.0.8 |

Build

Pushes to main run four jobs: arm64-control (upstream module, unchanged, catches regressions), x86_64-port (this port, android15-6.6), x86_64-matrix (the other KMIs the KernelSU-Next CI covers, android12-5.10 up to android17-6.18) and x86_64-package. All must be green. Artifacts per run: x86_64-android15-6.6-susfs_guard_lkm.ko, the per-KMI x86_64--susfs_guard_lkm.ko set, x86_64-susfs_sc (bare supercall test client) and x86_64-susfs-lkm-module (the flashable loader module zip, one .ko per KMI, the boot script picks by kernel release). Prebuilt binaries: the releases page.

Install

The module zip is the intended path: KernelSU-Next manager, module section, install from storage, reboot (or ksud module install susfs_lkm_x64.zip). After reboot the module loads itself at boot and installs the x86_64 susfs CLI at /data/adb/ksu/bin/susfs (with sus and ksu_susfs symlinks) for manager modules that call the classic command line. Check with ksud susfs version, expect v2.3.0.

For a manual one-shot load instead: plain insmod cannot work, five imports are unexported to modules on every GKI variant, arm64 included, same as upstream. Use ksud insmod . The module hides itself from lsmod on purpose; check /sys/module/susfs_guard_lkm instead.

State

Live-tested on the emulator: autoload after reboot, ksud susfs version answers v2.3.0 and ksud susfs support answers Supported, sus_path hides paths from app uids while root and shell still see them, uname spoof, kstat/opath/open_redirect tables, no-opt probes holding. v1 scope: the AArch32 compat layer stays arm64-only.

!image.png

Userspace talks through the reboot-ABI supercall and the /proc/susfs_* nodes (interface reference: upstream PROC_INTERFACES.md).

> IMPORTANT: Manager modules that ship their own arm64 susfs/ksu_susfs binaries (BRENE, sidex15) still carry a dead arm64 binary inside; the installed CLI here answers the same command surface, but those modules' installers may need their arch gate bypassed.

Short Answer: susfs4ksu-module and all its forks still needs to be ported to x86_64

Origin and license

Port of inforcqb/susfs4ksu-lkm, which ports simonpunk/susfs4ksu (logic and hook points), with patch_memory/lsm_hook/symbol_resolver from SukiSU-Ultra. GPL-2.0-only, see LICENSE. Research and learning only, use at your own risk.

Disclaimer

I am no developer or a low level programmer, I am a guy who loves breaking, testing, building security releated tools that helps with my workflow, excpect bugs and errors, thank you.
